solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part of film in France tormented mercenary

indicators.note: the film part sits inside the reworked country name, so 'in' signals placing one piece within another
something tormented is twisted and wrung about, so the letters of France are rearranged

parts.note: a reel is one spool or section of a film

explanation.surface: A tortured soldier of fortune appears in part of a French film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France' looks like a location after 'in', but it is the anagram fodder and 'in' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary works for whoever pays, the same as a self-employed hired hand with no fixed master.

clue.text: The Gunners draw contest for dominance

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
to draw an outline is to trace it

explanation.surface: Arsenal, nicknamed the Gunners, play out a draw in a battle for supremacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Gunners' suggests Arsenal football club, but here it is the Royal Artillery, RA.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a ruthless competitive struggle to get ahead, especially at work.

clue.text: Bass hiding in European sea plant

indicators.note: the bass letter is concealed within the sea's name, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A bass fish lurks among European seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' is a verb here: to fix firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to set it firmly into its surroundings, as a reporter is fixed within a military unit.

clue.text: Councillor and nearly all the foreign staff

indicators.note: nearly all of the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: der is German for 'the', so a foreign 'the'
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A local councillor, together with nearly all the overseas employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: In British local government a senior elected member of a borough council was given this title.

clue.text: Search one country to secure safe access?

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country
to lock something is to make it secure

explanation.surface: Instructions to scour a land in order to guarantee safe entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe' is a noun here, the strongbox, and the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox is opened by dialling the right sequence of numbers on its dial mechanism.

clue.text: Note upcoming cheese agent

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A memo about an ingredient for cheese-making that is due soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reverses TENNER in this down entry; a tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: This enzyme preparation curdles milk, the step that starts cheese-making.

clue.text: Churchwarden perhaps just beat earl

parts.note: to pip someone is to beat them narrowly

explanation.surface: A church official narrowly defeats a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchwarden' looks like a parish officer; it is also a long-stemmed clay smoking device, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchwarden is a long clay tobacco pipe, given as an example.

clue.text: It's fed to cat perhaps for keeping you sweet

indicators.note: the pronoun is given to the animal, so it follows straight after it

parts.note: a cat is an example of a pet
read as 'it is', it supplies IT

indicators.note: the word for holds the letter for you inside it

parts.note: taken as the word itself, f-o-r
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A tasty morsel given to the cat to keep you in its good books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts U inside FOR to make FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: These small fancy cakes or confections are served with coffee after a meal.

clue.text: Present teacher and revolutionary judge

parts.note: prof is short for professor, a university teacher

indicators.note: revolving turns the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a game

explanation.surface: A gift from a lecturer and a radical magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns REF into FER.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hold it out for acceptance, to offer it.

clue.text: End time in boat

indicators.note: the time letter is placed within the vessel

parts.note: a sub, or submarine, is a boat

explanation.surface: Finishing a spell aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short end left over, as of a cigarette or pencil.

clue.text: Party lackey impresses at authority

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the lackey holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a minion is a servile follower

explanation.surface: A party underling impresses at the seat of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impresses' is read literally as 'presses in': the lackey takes the next word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Domination is control or power over others, which is what authority gives.

clue.text: Stray rook follows opposite directions

indicators.note: the chess piece comes after the compass phrase

parts.note: west and east are opposite compass points: W and E
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A wayward chess rook heads off in opposite directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite directions' is W AND E, the word 'and' kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to roam aimlessly away from a set path.

clue.text: Finger impression provided in case of injury

indicators.note: the dent and condition sit within the outer letters
the case is the outside, so the first and last letters

parts.note: a dent is an impression in a surface
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A fingerprint is taken where there is an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finger' is a verb, to point out a culprit. 'case of' gives I and Y, the outside letters of 'injury'.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger a suspect is to name or point them out to the police.

clue.text: Rum old man hosts returning groups of soldiers

indicators.note: the father figure holds the army units inside him like guests

parts.note: da is an informal word for father, one's old man

indicators.note: the units come back, so they are read in reverse

parts.note: RA (Royal Artillery) and REME (Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers) are British Army corps

explanation.surface: A strange elderly man welcomes back troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the adjective 'strange'; it is the drink. RA and REME are British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a rum distilled in Guyana, named after its river region.

clue.text: Grinding gears tend to become separated

indicators.note: grinding gears grate and churn, so the letters are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: A car's crunching gearbox tends to fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged describes a couple or relatives who have become separated and no longer close.

clue.text: Ladies' fingers soak bread, missing odd bits

indicators.note: dropping the first, third, fifth and further odd-placed letters leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: A recipe step: soak the bread but leave out the odd crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies' fingers is another name for this green pod vegetable, used in gumbo.

clue.text: Insert line in notice for pedant

indicators.note: the instruction tells you to put the line letter into the notice

parts.note: a sticker is a small printed notice

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a line to a sign, fit for a fussy reader.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact rules, which is the mark of a pedant.

clue.text: Hill-dweller accommodates posh relative

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the insect holds the letter inside it

parts.note: an ant lives in an anthill
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A mountain resident puts up a well-to-do family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill-dweller' suggests a highlander but means an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family member.

clue.text: It's pointless wasting fluorine gas, for instance

indicators.note: to waste is to lose or squander, so the element's symbol is lost

parts.note: something pointless has futility, uselessness
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine

explanation.surface: Squandering fluorine gas is a futile exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' looks like the element but is the household supply; 'wasting' drops F.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas, water and electricity supplied to homes are each a public service of this kind.

clue.text: Break in travel for refreshment

indicators.note: to refresh is to renew, so the letters are made over into fresh order

explanation.surface: Pausing a journey for something to eat and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for refreshment' looks like a reason to stop; it is the anagram signal, acting on 'travel' only, with 'in' kept as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause between parts, as in a theatre, where drinks are served.

clue.text: We split apart, staggering

indicators.note: the pronoun breaks the other word open and sits in the gap

parts.note: read as 'a part', which is A plus SOME

explanation.surface: We broke up and are reeling from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart' must be read as two words, 'a part', with 'part' meaning some.
explanation.definitionFit: Something staggering is astonishing, inspiring wonder.

clue.text: Manage transport at university

parts.note: to bear is to carry or transport
being up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Running the transport at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' in British usage means attending university, as at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is to cope bravely under strain, to get by.

clue.text: Jack sliced fruit and chopped vegetable

indicators.note: the sailor cuts into the citrus fruit and sits within it

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman)

indicators.note: chopped short, the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Jack cut up fruit and diced vegetables in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name but is a sailor, the able seaman of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat pale legume, a butter bean, is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: You and I chase horse hitched to black trap

indicators.note: to chase is to follow, so the pronoun comes after the horse

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
together you and I are we
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: We pursue a horse harnessed to a dark carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' suggests a pony carriage in the scene but defines a spider's snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins this sticky silk net to snare insects.

clue.text: Edited UK-Arab article omitted religious coverage

indicators.note: edited text is reworked, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the article is left out of the letters before rearranging

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A British-Arab piece was edited, leaving out the religion coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coverage' is literal: a garment covering the body.
explanation.definitionFit: This full-body garment is worn by some Muslim women for religious modesty.

clue.text: After meal, hands in this brown gel if spoiled

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so the letters are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: After dinner, the diners rinse their hands in a bowl of spoiled brown jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Diners dip their fingers in this small dish of water at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Bouncer primarily manages space

parts.note: a roo, or kangaroo, bounces along

indicators.note: first of all, so just the opening letter

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman mainly controls the space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' looks like a doorman but is a kangaroo, ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means available space, as in room to move.

clue.text: Teetotal bishop repelled old scorer

indicators.note: driven back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: dry means abstaining from alcohol
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: An abstinent bishop drove off an elderly cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests a cricket scorer, but means a composer who writes scores.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was a Tudor composer, an old writer of musical scores.

clue.text: Impassive royal couple placed in stern

indicators.note: the royal pair are put inside the word for stern

parts.note: po-faced means humourlessly stern
a king, K, and a queen, ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: An unmoved royal couple set into a ship's stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like the back of a ship but means po-faced, British for disapprovingly serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impassive shows no emotion, keeping a blank expression as card players do.
